title: Probability: Two Events, Sample Spaces and Relative Frequency
seo_title: Grade 8 Probability Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Consider a simple situation (with equally probable outcomes) that can be described using probability; list all the possible outcomes; determine the probability of each possible outcome using the definition of probability; predict with reasons the relative frequency of the possible outcomes for a series of trials based on probability; compare relative frequency with probability and explain possible differences.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 8 probability worksheets: two dice, coins and spinners, sample spaces, Venn diagrams and two-way tables. 100 questions with memos.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • List all the outcomes in a table or a tree. Two dice give 36 outcomes.
  • Probability = favourable outcomes ÷ all outcomes.
  • P(not A) = 1 − P(A).
  • In a Venn diagram, count the overlap only once.

Examples

Example

Two dice: total of 7

6 ways out of 36

Answer: 1/6

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding instead of countingList the outcomes.
Missing outcomesUse a table.
The overlap twiceCount it once.

items.q: A class of 50 learners has 48 who play a musical instrument. A learner is chosen at random. What is the probability that the learner does NOT play an instrument?
items.e: 50 − 48 = 2 learners do not play, so the probability is 125.

items.q: A weather forecast gives a 41% chance of rain tomorrow. What is the chance it does not rain?
items.e: The chances add to 100%: 100% − 41% = 59%.

items.q: A weather forecast gives a 67% chance of rain tomorrow. What is the chance it does not rain?
